name: Basis point
title: Basis point: Meaning, Formula & Worked Example
description: A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point. Learn its formula, a 25-bps example and how it differs from relative percentage change.
definition: One basis point is 0.01 percentage point, so 25 bps equals 0.25% as a rate quantity and 0.0025 as a decimal. A move from 5% to 5.25% is a 25-bps absolute increase and a 5% relative increase. Use the mode that matches a conversion, a rate comparison or a proportional monetary amount.
explanation: A quoted percentage, a decimal fraction and a basis-point value can represent the same rate. Enter 25 with Basis points selected, 0.25 with Percent selected, or 0.0025 with Decimal selected to describe the same quantity. Entering 0.25 as a decimal instead describes 25%, or 2,500 bps. The input-unit selection is part of the calculation, not a cosmetic label.
formula: 1 basis point = 0.01 percentage point = 0.0001 decimal; bps of an amount = amount × bps / 10,000
formulaNote: Financial rate conversion and proportional amounts only. No live rates, compounding, mortgage payment calculation or implied time period. Relative rate change is shown only for a positive starting rate.

example.title: Convert 25 bps to 0.25% and 0.0025
steps: Divide 25 by 100 for the percent quantity; divide by 10,000 for the decimal fraction.
example.answer: The equivalents are 0.25% and 0.0025; the original quantity remains 25 bps.
example.assumptions: Financial rate conversion and proportional amounts only. No live rates, compounding, mortgage payment calculation or implied time period. Relative rate change is shown only for a positive starting rate.

pitfall.title: Does 25 bps on a mortgage equal a $500 payment change?
pitfall.text: On a fixed $200,000 base, 25 bps represents $500 of proportional amount. That is not a change in monthly mortgage payment; an amortizing payment also depends on the term, balance and payment frequency.

scope: Financial rate conversion and proportional amounts only. No live rates, compounding, mortgage payment calculation or implied time period. Relative rate change is shown only for a positive starting rate.

guides.title: Basis Points vs. Percentage Points: Convert Rates Without Mixing Units

questions.question: How many basis points are in 1%?
questions.answer: A 1% rate quantity equals 100 basis points. A change of one percentage point also equals 100 bps; a 1% relative increase is a different comparison.

questions.question: Is 25 bps the same as 0.25%?
questions.answer: Yes as a rate quantity: 25 bps = 0.25% = 0.0025 in decimal form. A 25-bps change means 0.25 percentage point, not necessarily a 0.25% relative change.

name: Prorated rent
title: Prorated rent: Meaning, Formula & Worked Example
description: Prorated rent is a charge for part of a billing period. See a monthly-rent example, day-count choices and the limits of the calculation.
definition: Prorated rent charges only the selected billable days. With $2,000 monthly rent and January 17–31 included, the actual-calendar calculation is $2,000 / 31 × 15 = $967.74. A 30-day denominator gives $1,000 for the same dates. Use the method and billable-date convention required by your agreement and applicable rules.
explanation: A move date alone may not tell you which days are chargeable. The calculator asks for the first and last billable days and includes both. January 17 through January 31 contains fifteen billable days. If an agreement excludes the departure day, enter the day before departure rather than silently treating the displayed end date as exclusive.
formula: Prorated rent = selected monthly or annual rent base / denominator days × billable days; sum date segments without intermediate rounding
formulaNote: Manual constant monthly rent and explicitly included billable dates. The selected day-count method is an assumption, not a legal ruling or a determination of lease obligations. No deposits, utilities, concessions or automatic monthly caps.

example.title: Fifteen January days at $2,000 monthly rent
example.intro: $2,000.00 monthly rent; 2026-01-17 through 2026-01-31, both included; Actual days in each month.
steps: January has 31 days and the included interval has 15.
Multiply the unrounded $2,000 / 31 daily rate by 15.
example.answer: Estimated rent is $967.74 after final rounding.
example.assumptions: Manual constant monthly rent and explicitly included billable dates. The selected day-count method is an assumption, not a legal ruling or a determination of lease obligations. No deposits, utilities, concessions or automatic monthly caps.

expected.label: Estimated rent for selected billable days

pitfall.title: Why can my invoice differ by a few cents?
pitfall.text: The worksheet keeps full daily-rate precision and rounds the final total for display. An invoice that rounds each daily charge or each monthly line before summing can differ; use the agreed rounding policy.

tools.text: Use the stated units and assumptions to explore this definition with the calculator.

scope: Manual constant monthly rent and explicitly included billable dates. The selected day-count method is an assumption, not a legal ruling or a determination of lease obligations. No deposits, utilities, concessions or automatic monthly caps.

guides.title: How to Prorate Rent: Actual Days, 30-Day Months & Leap Years

questions.question: Do I count the move-in and move-out days?
questions.answer: This calculator includes both entered billable dates. Whether a departure day is chargeable depends on your agreement and applicable rules. If it is excluded, enter the preceding day as the last billable day.

questions.question: Should I divide rent by 30 or by the days in the month?
questions.answer: Use the method applicable to your agreement. Actual-calendar, fixed-30-day and annual methods can differ. The calculator displays the selected method and does not determine which one is legally required.

name: Operating cash flow
title: Operating cash flow: Meaning, Formula & Worked Example
description: Operating cash flow measures cash generated or used by operating activities. Learn its formula, a checked example and how OCF differs from profit.
definition: Operating cash flow measures cash generated or used by the entered operating activities. In the worked reconciliation, $120,000 net income plus $30,000 adjustments minus a $20,000 operating working-capital increase gives $130,000 OCF. The same result can be reconstructed from consistent operating cash receipts and payments; it is not the same measure as profit or free cash flow.
explanation: Accrual earnings and operating cash answer different questions. A credit sale can enter revenue before collection; depreciation can reduce earnings without a current-period cash payment. A useful reconciliation identifies the specific items separating the two measures instead of assuming net income is money available in a bank account.
formula: Indirect OCF = net income + signed noncash / nonoperating adjustments − increase in operating net working capital; direct OCF = operating receipts − operating payments
formulaNote: A manual operating-cash-flow worksheet for one consistent reporting scope. Inputs require reconciled classifications; the tool does not prepare a complete accounting statement, retrieve company accounts or calculate free cash flow.

example.title: Reconcile $120,000 net income to $130,000 operating cash flow
example.intro: Same period: net income $120,000; adjustments $30,000; operating asset increases $15,000 receivables, $10,000 inventory and $5,000 other; operating liability increases $8,000 payables and $2,000 other.
steps: Operating asset increases use $30,000 cash; operating liability increases release $10,000.
example.answer: OCF is $130,000; the positive $20,000 net working-capital increase is a cash use.
example.assumptions: A manual operating-cash-flow worksheet for one consistent reporting scope. Inputs require reconciled classifications; the tool does not prepare a complete accounting statement, retrieve company accounts or calculate free cash flow.

expected.label: Operating cash flow under entered assumptions

pitfall.title: Is operating cash flow the same as free cash flow?
pitfall.text: No. Capital expenditure is a separate investing cash-flow item. Free cash flow commonly adjusts operating cash flow for capital spending, but definitions vary and this calculator does not label OCF as free cash flow.

questions.question: What is the operating cash flow formula?
questions.answer: In this indirect worksheet, start with net income, add signed noncash and nonoperating reconciliation adjustments, then subtract the increase in operating net working capital. Direct mode subtracts operating cash payments from operating receipts.

questions.question: Does an increase in accounts receivable add or subtract cash?
questions.answer: An included operating receivables increase is subtracted in the indirect reconciliation. A decrease is entered as a negative change and adds cash, assuming the change has been reconciled for noncash and nonoperating movements.
